queue.recognise: You can recognise it by the trunk, six metres round inside a light protective fence, with two limbs resting on props. It stands beside the ruins of the Chapelle de Saint-Jammes on the D45 between Sorèze and Arfons.
queue.story:
The town of Sorèze gives this beech a crown ninety metres across, close to the length of a football pitch, carried on a trunk six metres round. It is roughly 450 years old and twenty metres tall, and two of its great limbs now rest on props.

It grows high on the Montagne Noire beside the ruins of the Chapelle de Saint-Jammes, a pre-Romanesque chapel of the eleventh century with an old cemetery at its side, on ground that once belonged to the Prats Vieils estate. The spot lay on a route of the Way of St James, so for much of the tree's life the people passing under it were pilgrims bound for Compostela. The chapel is now a ruin. The beech is not, and local tradition has kept its own legends
queue.name: The Multisecular Beech of Saint-Jammes
